title: Skydance Bonds Extend Losses Amid Warner Bros. Buyout Angst
summary: Skydance Corp. bonds weakened further on Tuesday, and the cost of protecting the company’s debt against default jumped, as investors fretted about the profitability of the company after its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc.

title: The Benefit of Free After-School Programs
summary: There’s one public policy that offers clear advantages to the old-timers and youngsters alike: government-funded, universal after-school programs. In a world of hard problems, this is an easy win, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Kathryn Anne Edwards explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wells Fargo CFO on Earnings, Deals, Consumer Strength
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. Chief Financial Officer Mike Santomassimo says they've seen "good activity" across different parts of the business. He talks about lending, interest rates and deals activity on "Bloomberg The Close." Third-quarter results topped Wall Street estimates as consumers and businesses held steady. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: NYC Horse Carriages Set to Be Banned in 2028 After Deal
summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the New York City Council speaker reached a deal on legislation to ban horse-drawn carriages, potentially putting an end to a Central Park staple and tourist magnet that began operating more than 150 years ago.

title: Ancora in Push for UK’s Big Yellow Group to Explore Sale
summary: Activist investor Ancora Holdings Group has built a stake in UK-listed Big Yellow Group Plc and is pushing the self-storage company to explore a sale, according to a statement from the fund.

title: Aramco Headquarters Hit During Houthi Attack on Saudi Arabia
summary: Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran in eastern Saudi Arabia was hit during a missile attack by Yemen’s Houthi militants on Tuesday that caused a fire in a part of the complex, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: Higher Rates Turbocharge Lending Income for Biggest US Banks
summary: Three of the biggest US banks set a fresh record in the third quarter for how much they earned from lending, with customers continuing to borrow even as interest rates increased. Norah Mulinda has more.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bull Market Has Room to Run, Says Truist's Keith Lerner
summary: Stocks bounced from session lows as speculation the Federal Reserve won’t be forced to raise rates aggressively offset lingering worries about elevated oil prices and the outlook for artificial intelligence. Keith Lerner, CIO and chief market strategist at Truist Advisory Services, says the four-year-old bull market has room to run, with AI and technology still central to its prospects. He speaks with hosts Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec on Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Selloff Drags Emerging Stocks Down, Weighs on Currency Gauge
summary: The deepening selloff in shares linked to artificial intelligence dragged emerging-market equities down for their worst day since July.

title: Stocks Bounce From Lows on Williams’ Rate Remarks: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks bounced from session lows as speculation the Federal Reserve won’t be forced to raise rates aggressively offset lingering worries about elevated oil prices and the outlook for artificial intelligence.

title: Sheinbaum Vows to Buy More From US to Reach Trump Trade Deal
summary: President Claudia Sheinbaum said her government is addressing Donald Trump’s concerns about the growing US trade deficit with Mexico by buying more American goods as she pushes to secure a deal with Washington.

title: S&P 500 Closes Flat as Bank Earnings Kick Off, Chipmakers Slide
summary: US stocks held steady in another session of becalmed trading on Tuesday, as weakness in chipmakers continued and traders sorted through generally robust results from JPMorgan Chase & Co., Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and other lenders in the start to third-quarter corporate earnings season.

title: Bumble Surges 56% on $1.3 Billion Take-Private Deal | Closing Bell
summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Scarlet Fu, Hema Parmar, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Microsoft Hits First Record in a Year After $1.4 Trillion Rally
summary: Microsoft Corp. shares hit their first record in about a year Tuesday as the software maker’s four-month rally gains momentum.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 13
summary: Oil held steady after three sessions of gains as traders booked profits from the recent rally while threats to energy supplies continued to loom from the Middle East to Russia.

title: Copper Slips as AI Selloff Saps Appetite for Risk Across Markets
summary: Copper wavered as traders weighed investor angst around overheated spending on metal-intensive AI infrastructure against continued supply risks.

title: Chile: AFP sufren pérdidas por apuestas a tasas de EE.UU.
summary: La apuesta por una caída de las tasas no dio resultado. Ahora las AFP deben reducir sus posiciones en derivados justo cuando cerrar esos contratos resulta más costoso.

title: Get Ready for the Chinese Data Center Ramp
summary: Let’s see how fast China catches up.

title: Gold Pares Losses as Fed’s Williams Signals 2027 End to Hikes
summary: Gold pared losses after Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said he still sees one more interest-rate hike as appropriate this year, but doesn’t expect further tightening in 2027.

title: Trump Says US Still Sharing Intelligence With Ukraine
summary: Kelly Grieco, a senior fellow at global research firm the Stimson Center, said a ceasefire on attacking energy infrastructure between Russia and Ukraine benefits the Russians more as the country is able to sell oil to fund the war. Grieco said that even if Ukraine is not able to hit Russian energy infrastructure there are still ways to inflict damage including hitting at travel hubs like airports.  (Source: Bloomberg)
